results.source: historical_cases#H-05 Three sensors offline at once
results.text: Three sensors in different rooms went offline at the same minute; base station online, RSSI history normal, E-610 in log. Restarting did not help. Escalated; radio module replaced. Escalated correctly.

Peripherals talk to the base station over a sub-GHz proprietary radio. Signal strength (RSSI) is shown in Device Settings > Device Info. Above -70 dBm is good, -70 to -80 dBm is acceptable, below -80 dBm causes intermittent disconnections, delayed notifications and choppy live view. Concrete walls, metal doors and fridges strongly attenuate the signal. Fix: move the device or base station, or install the official RP-1 repeater.
Customer reported a CAM-S1 in a detached garage going offline several times a day. RSSI was -86 dBm; all other devices normal. Installing an RP-1 repeater solved it. Resolved at frontline.

results.text: The base station could not write the new binding into its binding table. A single occurrence can follow a power interruption during pairing; retry once after restarting the base station. If E-207 repeats, or the app lists a device that the base station table does not contain, the binding table is likely corrupted: escalate to FAE. Do not factory-reset the base station.

Hold SYNC for 15 seconds until the LED flashes white. This removes the peripheral's own binding but does not remove it from the base station table; remove it in the app first, then reset, then pair again.
